_comment: CAPT-W4-ERP 2026-08-12: was keyed on `operation_id`, which /api/operations does NOT serve (16 fields, measured: order_id, production_order_no, operation_number, vorgangs_nr, work_center, machine_id, status, qty_planned, qty_done, qty_scrap, started_at, ended_at, planned_start, planned_end, setup_minutes, cycle_time_seconds). Activating the source in that state would have emitted ZERO events for every row. The static key linter could not see it: idProperty == isId == a declared column is INTERNALLY consistent, and the declaration was simply wrong about what the upstream serves - only LINT_SOURCE_KEYS_LIVE=1 catches this class (K1/L1). Re-keyed onto the composite that IS unique upstream: (production_order_no, operation_number) = 200/200 distinct, 0 rows with an empty part, while production_order_no alone is only 60/200. This needs NOTHING from sim-v5 - the previous comment asked for operation_id to be added upstream, which is unnecessary. it-edge supports composite keys on the REST path (poller.ts primaryKeyColumns / encodeCompositePk, both present in the running it-edge:0.4.1 image). STILL NOT in it-edge SOURCE_IDS - activating is a separate decision. CAPT-RETRACT 2026-08-18: polling ADDED with paginate true, changeDetection full_refresh, batchSize 5000 and an EXPLICIT intervalMs. VERDICT: LATENT-BUT-DECLARED, and the latency is verified rather than assumed - this sourceId appears in NO it-edge SOURCE_IDS. Read off the three running containers on .99: osf-it-edge-erp carries erp-production-orders, erp-operations-response, erp-bde-confirmations, sim-v5-erp-articles, sim-v5-erp-customers, sim-v5-erp-calendar; osf-it-edge-qms carries sim-v5-qms-inspections; osf-it-edge-wms carries sim-v5-wms-quants. So this source has never emitted a DATA-7 refusal and NO refusal count is claimed for it - the defect was latent and so is the fix. What the fix prevents: the moment this source is activated, it-edge (DATA-7) would refuse every delete/tombstone pass with reason unpaginated_full_refresh, so it could ingest but never RETRACT and an operation deleted upstream would stay in the KG for ever. MEASURED BEFORE against the live ERP .154:38260, with /api/orders?limit=5 -> 5 as the positive control in the same run: baseline -> 200, ?limit=3 -> 3 (honoured), ?offset=99999 -> 200, ?page_size=7 -> 200, ?page=2 -> 200. Half-implemented paging is MORE dangerous than none: the obvious test (limit) passes, while it-edge stops paging only on an EMPTY page and advances the offset by the rows actually returned, so it would have re-fetched page one up to MAX_PAGES=10000 times per poll and still reported pagination_truncated. offset is the decider, never limit. AND THERE IS A TRAP INSIDE THAT TRAP: ?offset=99999 -> 200 is NOT by itself proof that offset was ignored. erp.order_operations holds 268,562 rows, so offset 99999 legitimately still has rows behind it, and that probe returns 200 both BEFORE and AFTER the fix for opposite reasons. The conclusive before-evidence is the upstream statement itself (LIMIT $1, no OFFSET clause, a single-element parameter list - offset never reached the SQL); the conclusive after-evidence is an offset BEYOND the population plus page disjointness. Fixed upstream: sim-v5 api-erp d079f0ce (F-OPERATIONS-PAGINATION), deployed to PROD as image tag 103145bd. VERIFIED ON PROD, same positive control in the same run: ?limit=3 -> 3, ?page_size=7 -> 7 (was 200), ?limit=99999 -> 5000 (the cap, was 1000), ?limit=10&offset=268000 -> 10, ?limit=10&offset=400000 -> 0 (the empty page it-edge needs in order to stop), and the pages at offset 0 and offset 3 are DISJOINT - 0 overlap, monotone key order. PAGING EXHAUSTS THE POPULATION EXACTLY, at TWO page sizes, paged the way it-edge pages: batchSize 5000 -> 55 pages (54 full plus the empty terminator), 268,560 rows / 268,560 distinct / 0 duplicates; batchSize 2000 -> 136 pages, 268,562 / 268,562 distinct / 0 duplicates. Both runs matched the authoritative count read from erp.order_operations at the same moment (268,560 and 268,562; the table was stable at 268,562 across the second run). ORDERING WAS THE REAL RISK AND IT NEEDED AN UPSTREAM CHANGE, not merely an OFFSET: the historical ORDER BY leads with actual_start DESC, which MUTATES - when an operation starts its row jumps from the NULLS-LAST tail to the head and shifts every row behind it by one, so a page-through under that key SKIPS rows, and for a full_refresh source a skipped row is a FALSE RETRACTION, not a cosmetic glitch. Upstream now orders a PAGED read by (production_order_no, operation_number) - exactly this source primaryKeyColumns, and a total order over the whole table (268,562 rows / 268,562 distinct, measured) - while an UNPAGED read keeps the documented recency top-N ordering unchanged. intervalMs IS SET HERE, DELIBERATELY, unlike sim-v5-erp-articles/customers which stay on the 30 s default: a complete poll of this source is 268,562 rows at a measured 458 bytes/row = about 123 MB and 55 requests, which on a 30 s cadence would be roughly 4 MB/s sustained against .154, a host that is already overloaded. At 900000 ms it is 55 requests and about 123 MB per quarter hour. WHOEVER ACTIVATES THIS SOURCE MUST RE-PRICE THAT before doing so: the number to check is the POPULATION, not the flag.
